A.reason: All candidates preserve traceability, require no purchase, specify reversible procedures and measure the required outcomes over two weeks. Candidate 7 refines candidate 0's acceptance mechanism; interruption recovery does not make it a separate primary mechanism. The other groups target stable placement, serial labeling, fewer custody changes, spreadsheet key association, obsolete-label control, processing restart and fewer container changes. Candidate 7 is strongest because it directly addresses handoffs, assigns custody until acceptance, contains mismatches and provides inspectable checks and rollback.

B.reason: All candidates meet the hard constraints and provide reversible, measurable trials. Their primary mechanisms are source-checked acceptance, stable placement, serial labeling, fewer custody changes and batch identifier reconciliation. Candidate 0 offers the strongest direct fit to handoff errors with modest existing-resource requirements, independent source verification and documented mismatch handling.

pair.reason: A7 narrowly improves on B0 by specifying who retains custody during interrupted or ambiguous acceptance and requiring a restarted check before processing. That closes a concrete handoff gap while preserving traceability, measuring waiting costs and providing explicit recovery. Effectiveness remains unproven in both proposals.
